trades.holding_period_note: sessions_held is measured per closed tranche of an average-cost lot, so tranches of the same lot share its entry date and their intervals overlap; they must not be summed. sessions_in_market is the union.

costs.note_price_difference: slippage_bps / price_difference is measured against the decision mid and therefore INCLUDES intraday drift (it can be negative). execution_cost_bps is friction only.

implementation_shortfall.note: drift is the mid's own movement between decision and execution; it is a timing outcome, not a fee, and is reported separately from the friction components.

pnl_decomposition.note: Realized and open P&L are net of explicit cash costs (commission, exchange and regulatory fees less rebates), which are the only costs charged to cash separately; spread, depth and impact are already inside the fill prices. The residual is the rounding gap and is reported rather than hidden.

narrative.headline: Beat the market: +158.09% total return vs +14.41% for the index, +105.11pp residual after beta, -55.0% max drawdown, 0.68% of capital lost to execution costs.

clauses.text: Finished at +158.09% against the S&P 500's +14.41% over the same 251 sessions - an excess return of +143.68pp.
The beta premium this participant is built to harvest was live (+35.95% over the season) and the account made money - a tailwind that cannot be separated from skill on one path.
The momentum premium went against the declared exposure (-7.04% for a +0.5 loading) yet the account still returned +158.09% - the result was driven by something other than this factor.
Of the +158.09% total, about +52.98pp is explained by carrying beta 3.68 against a +14.41% market (R^2 0.20); the residual +105.11pp is everything else - selection, timing, leverage and cost.
CVNA contributed +159,044 USD (101% of net P&L) across 3 closed trades; META was the biggest drag at -63,865 USD.
Execution cost 684 USD (0.68% of starting capital, 1.2 bp per fill, 1.3 bp of the 5,428,866 USD traded). 89% of that was spread/depth/impact and 11% was explicit fees and rebates.
7 closed round trips, 71.4% winners, profit factor 3.20, average winner +45,566 vs average loser -35,653 USD, median holding 31 sessions.

Time in market, measured without double counting: 251 sessions held at least one position (the per-tranche holding periods above sum to 274 sessions because tranches of the same average-cost lot share its entry date, so they overlap and must not be added together).
Single worst trade: META long 2026-08-21 to 2026-09-16, -63,865 USD.
Worst peak-to-trough drawdown -54.98% (-9.10% for the index), trough on 2026-07-29, never recovered. Average gross exposure 419% of starting capital, peak leverage 2.57x.
Daily returns were +1.12 skewed with excess kurtosis +6.63; historical 95% VaR -9.20%/day with CVaR -13.30%/day. Worst single session -24.72%, best +41.54%.

The style premia quoted above are measured on the simulated replay, whose cross-sectional drifts are DECLARED scenario parameters (see sim/universe.py). They describe this competition, not the real market: IR-16.

Declared failure mode(s) this run CANNOT test, because no measurable condition matches their wording (they are neither confirmed nor ruled out): The switching threshold creates hysteresis, so it holds losers too long; No diversification means the outcome is almost entirely one idiosyncratic draw.

prose.title: Mandate (as declared before the season)
prose.text: @OneBigBet_Concentra (One Big Bet) ran the "concentration" archetype. Declared thesis: Diversification dilutes return. Put the entire account, at maximum leverage, into the single name with the best risk-scaled 63-session momentum, and switch only when another name is materially better. Entry: Score every name by 63-session momentum divided by realised volatility; Hold only the top name at 2.0x gross; Switch only if the runner-up's score exceeds the incumbent's by more than 0.5. Exit: Switch, or the mandatory end-of-season liquidation. Sizing: 200% of equity in one name. Leverage: 2.0x gross, one position. Cadence: daily check, rare switches, horizon weeks to months. Aggression 5/5. This participant was built to maximise return, not to manage risk: The mathematically highest-variance legal book in the competition, which is what a highest-return-only mandate implies.
